title: Cartier line bundle and canonical section under Cartier preserving pullback
statement: Let $h:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $D\hookrightarrow T$ be an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Assume the scheme-theoretic pullback $D'=T'\times_TD$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is again an effective Cartier divisor. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $h^*\mathcal O_T(D)\cong\mathcal O_{T'}(D')$, where the divisor line bundles and module pullback are [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle, def-pc-module-pullback], carrying the canonical section of $\mathcal O_T(D)$ to the canonical section of $\mathcal O_{T'}(D')$. On the complements, this isomorphism carries the canonical trivialization to the pulled-back trivialization. Here the canonical section of $\mathcal O_T(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ is the dual of the ideal inclusion $\mathcal I_D\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_T$; on $T-D$ it is a basis and defines the stated trivialization, and likewise on $T'-D'$.

proof.text: Choose an open cover $(U_i)$ of $T$ on which $\mathcal I_D=f_i\mathcal O_{U_i}$ with $f_i$ a non-zero-divisor, using [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Multiplication by $f_i$ identifies $\mathcal O_{U_i}$ with $\mathcal I_D|_{U_i}$: its inverse sends $a f_i$ to $a$, uniquely since $f_i$ is regular. Write $e_i$ for the dual basis, so $e_i(f_i)=1$. By [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], $\mathcal O_T(D)|_{U_i}=\mathcal O_{U_i}e_i$. The canonical section, which is the inclusion $\mathcal I_D\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_T$ viewed in its dual, is $f_i e_i$.

source.place: Tag 0C4U, lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-divisors (proof omitted); explicit local-equation proof using definition-invertible-sheaf-effective-Cartier-divisor

proof.text: Put $V_i=h^{-1}U_i$ and $g_i=h^\sharp(f_i)$. The tensor formula of [def-pc-module-pullback] and the structure-sheaf identification of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf] give bases $1\otimes f_i$ of $h^*\mathcal I_D|_{V_i}$ and $E_i=1\otimes e_i$ of $h^*\mathcal O_T(D)|_{V_i}$. Explicitly, on a trivializing open the coefficient isomorphism is $b\otimes a\mapsto b h^\sharp(a)$, with inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$; the tensor balancing relation proves they are inverses. The pulled-back ideal inclusion sends $1\otimes f_i$ to $g_i$. Apply [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image] to $D\hookrightarrow T$ and $h$. It identifies $\mathcal I_{D'}|_{V_i}$ with the image of this map, hence with $g_i\mathcal O_{V_i}$. This identifies the actual ideal of the scheme-theoretic fibre product, without assuming $h$ flat.

source.place: Tag 0C4U, lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-divisors (proof omitted); explicit local-equation proof using definition-invertible-sheaf-effective-Cartier-divisor

proof.text: The Cartier hypothesis on $D'$ ensures that $g_i$ is a free generator of its ideal, not merely a generator with a possible annihilator. Indeed refine $V_i$ by opens on which $\mathcal I_{D'}=(a)$ with $a$ regular. Since $(g_i)=(a)$, locally write $g_i=u a$ and $a=v g_i$. Then $(1-vu)a=0$, so $vu=1$. Thus $u$ is a unit and $g_i$ is regular. Multiplication by $g_i$ identifies $\mathcal O$ with $\mathcal I_{D'}$ on these opens, and these coefficient inverses agree wherever defined because their composites with the ideal inclusion do. Consequently $g_i$ is a basis on $V_i$ itself. Its dual $e'_i$ with $e'_i(g_i)=1$ is a basis of $\mathcal O_{T'}(D')|_{V_i}$, and the canonical section is $g_i e'_i$. This uses only the local-generator definition [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] and the dual definition [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle].

source.place: Tag 0C4U, lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-divisors (proof omitted); explicit local-equation proof using definition-invertible-sheaf-effective-Cartier-divisor

proof.text: Define an isomorphism on $V_i$ by $\theta_i(b E_i)=b e'_i$; its inverse sends $b e'_i$ to $b E_i$. Check overlaps explicitly. On $U_i\cap U_j$ the two ideal bases satisfy $f_i=u_{ij}f_j$ for a unique unit $u_{ij}$: write each basis in the other and cancel the regular generator to see the two coefficients multiply to $1$. Their dual bases satisfy $e_i=u_{ij}^{-1}e_j$. After pullback $E_i=h^\sharp(u_{ij})^{-1}E_j$ and $g_i=h^\sharp(u_{ij})g_j$, so $e'_i=h^\sharp(u_{ij})^{-1}e'_j$. Therefore $\theta_i$ and $\theta_j$ agree on the basis $E_i$ of their common restriction, and their inverses agree as well. These are direct changes of basis in the modules defined by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle, def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Tag 0C4U, lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-divisors (proof omitted); explicit local-equation proof using definition-invertible-sheaf-effective-Cartier-divisor

proof.text: The opens $V_i$ cover $T'$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] to the two global $\mathcal O_{T'}$-modules and the compatible maps $\theta_i$, and again to their inverses. This gives global maps $\theta$ and $\psi$. Their composites restrict to the identity on every $V_i$, so the uniqueness clause of the same lemma gives $\psi\theta=1$ and $\theta\psi=1$. Thus $\theta:h^*\mathcal O_T(D)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{T'}(D')$. For any other choice of local equations or any refinement, the overlap calculation of step 4 applies to the old and new bases on their common refinement. Hence the glued isomorphism is independent of these choices, by the same uniqueness clause. This proves canonicity, rather than merely existence of some isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04TN, lemma-glue-maps; module form and uniqueness as in lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules

proof.text: On $V_i$ the pullback of the canonical section $f_i e_i$ is $g_i E_i$ by the tensor balancing relation in [def-pc-module-pullback]. The defining formula for $\theta_i$ sends it to $g_i e'_i$, exactly the canonical section of $D'$ computed in step 3 using [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Equality on this covering implies equality of the global sections, since these modules are sheaves. On $U_i\setminus D$ the function $f_i$ is a unit, and its pullback $g_i$ is a unit on $V_i\setminus D'$: the closed subscheme on $V_i$ has ideal $(g_i)$ by step 2, so this complement is the locus where $g_i$ is invertible. Thus both canonical sections are bases there. Their preservation says explicitly that the trivializations $a\mapsto a\,1_D$ and $b\mapsto b\,1_{D'}$ commute with $\theta$ and pullback. This proves the final clause, including the empty-divisor and empty-complement cases.

Step 5: only clause (1) of the gluing node (glued morphisms and their uniqueness) is used. Step 6: the pullback of the canonical section is sent to the canonical section of D'. I recomputed every calculation. Edge cases checked: D empty, T' empty, and a non-flat map Z[t]->F_p[t].
